title: Linux_NyaDrop_Incident_Response_Scenario_111
description: Investigate and respond to a potential security incident involving the Linux/NyaDrop malware.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target system has exhibited unusual network activity. Your task is to investigate and respond to this potential security incident involving the Linux/NyaDrop malware. Learning objective: Gain hands-on experience in investigating and responding to a security incident involving the Linux/NyaDrop malware.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system is named `target` and is part of the 192.168.50.0/24 network. Enter the word 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system is named `target` and is part of the 192.168.50.0/24 network. Enter the word 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Investigate Unusual Network Activity
levels.content: Investigate the unusual network activity on the target system. Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service running on the target system. Look for the flag 'nyadrop_listener' in the output of the command.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, use the command `ss -tulnp | grep 4444`. The flag 'nyadrop_listener' will be present in the output if the service is running.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Start by checking the running services and network connections on the target system.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to list all running services and network connections.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Filter the output using the command `ss -tulnp | grep 4444` to identify the suspicious service. Look for the flag 'nyadrop_listener' in the output.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. Identify persistence mechanisms (e.g., systemd, cron, scheduled task). Look for the flag 'nyadrop.service' in the output of the command.
levels.solution: To identify the persistence mechanism, use the command `systemctl list-unit-files | grep nyadrop`. The flag 'nyadrop.service' will be present in the output if the service is configured to start automatically.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Start by checking the systemd services and timers on the target system.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-unit-files` to list all systemd services and timers.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Filter the output using the command `systemctl list-unit-files | grep nyadrop` to identify the persistence mechanism. Look for the flag 'nyadrop.service' in the output.

levels.title: Investigate Lateral Movement
levels.content: Investigate the file transfers or remote execution used to move between hosts. Correlate events across hosts to identify attacker lateral movement. Look for the flag 'payload-transfer.service' in the output of the command.
levels.solution: To investigate the lateral movement, use the command `journalctl -u payload-transfer.service`. The flag 'payload-transfer.service' will be present in the output if the service is used for lateral movement.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Start by checking the logs and network connections on both the target and next-target systems.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `journalctl -u payload-transfer.service` to investigate the lateral movement.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for the flag 'payload-transfer.service' in the output of the command.
